title: Making Temporal Betweenness Computation Faster and Restless

problem.claim: Computing betweenness for all nodes in temporal graphs is computationally hard for foremost and fastest paths, while existing solvable cases have high time complexity.

gap.claim: Prior restless-walk computation was known only for the shortest criterion and had complexity O(n^2 M T^2).

contributions.claim: Introduces an algorithm for temporal betweenness computation that uses O(n + M) space for shortest and shortest foremost paths and improves the prior algorithm's time complexity.
Extends temporal betweenness computation to restless walks with waiting constraints, providing a polynomial-time algorithm of complexity O(nM) for several optimality criteria.
Evaluates the algorithm across waiting constraints, optimisation criteria, and six public transit networks.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper explicitly introduces a new algorithm for temporal betweenness computation and extends it to restless walks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their algorithm performs between twice and almost 250 times better than the algorithm of Buß et al.
The authors report computing exact temporal betweenness values for several large temporal graphs with more than a million temporal edges.
The authors report general consistency among betweenness variants, but also a noticeable influence of waiting constraints and low correlation for some criterion pairs in some networks.

narrative_sequence.summary: Prior work established hardness for some temporal-path variants and a high-complexity algorithm for others.
The paper introduces a faster temporal betweenness algorithm and extends it to restless walks.
Experiments compare performance, scale to large temporal graphs, and examine waiting constraints and optimisation criteria.
The reported results show broad consistency across variants alongside meaningful effects of waiting constraints and some low correlations.

source_observation.claim: Changing waiting constraints can materially affect temporal betweenness and can reduce correlation between criteria in some networks.

interpretation.claim: Temporal centrality results may depend substantially on the operational rules governing movement and waiting.

application.claim: When applying temporal centrality to network data, evaluate multiple waiting constraints and optimisation criteria rather than relying on one default variant.

exception.claim: The reported low correlations occur only for certain pairs of criteria in some networks.

source_observation.claim: The algorithm reportedly enables exact computation on temporal graphs with more than a million temporal edges, whereas prior work allowed only approximate computation at that size.

interpretation.claim: Improving computational complexity can change temporal-centrality analysis from approximate to exact at larger graph sizes.

application.claim: Use complexity improvements to reassess whether exact centrality computation is feasible on large temporal datasets.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish exact feasibility for all temporal graph sizes or all path criteria.

unknowns: The exact time-complexity expression for shortest and shortest foremost paths is missing from S3.
The abstract does not specify the six transit networks beyond examples or provide experimental settings and datasets in detail.
